question: Should ambiguous Vault 403 responses continue to remain owner-scoped when token introspection is denied or unavailable, with provider aggregation reserved for positively evidenced shared outages?
rationale: This is an upgrade-sensitive diagnostic and authentication-classification contract: choosing the wrong default can misclassify legitimate path ACL failures or preserve misleading duplicate outage reports.

options.title: Confirm conservative classification
options.body: Approve the branch’s rule that ambiguous 403s stay ref-scoped while explicit shared authentication, bootstrap, transport, or availability failures aggregate by provider.

options.title: Require broader outage classification
options.body: Request a revised, documented rule if maintainers want certain ambiguous token failures to aggregate despite the risk of masking path-level ACL configuration.

recommendation.title: Confirm conservative classification
recommendation.body: Approve the branch’s rule that ambiguous 403s stay ref-scoped while explicit shared authentication, bootstrap, transport, or availability failures aggregate by provider.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor supplied the implementation, focused tests, and evidence for the exact Vault classification boundary under review.
